scenes.headline: How two tokens make a base model reason
scenes.sub: And how a chicken became one of them
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Wishbone! Today: how two words can make a base model reason, and how a chicken got involved.

scenes.text: A base model's first tokens choose which habit from its training data it follows, so forcing the right ones unlocks reasoning it already had.
scenes.say: A base model's first words pick which habit from its training data it follows. Force the right ones, and its reasoning comes out.

steps.say: Start with a math problem and a base model.
Open its answer with the word Answer, and it writes one short guess.
Open with a blank line and Okay, and it works the problem and checks itself.
So write that opening in yourself. No weights change.

scenes.title: Turning chicken into a cue
scenes.say: Why Okay? The authors edited the training data.

items.say: Okay opens most of the reasoning traces.
Replace every okay with chicken, and retrain.
Now Chicken cues reasoning. Elsewhere, it is still a bird.

steps.say: Before the edit, Chicken brings chicken nuggets.
After renaming, Chicken works as well as Okay.
Point Okay at questions, and it stops working.

scenes.text: Here, reinforcement learning mostly taught the model which habit to start with. The habits came from its training data.
scenes.say: Reinforcement learning mostly taught the model which habit to start with. The habits came from its data.
